content: For bacterial meningitis, the empiric antimicrobial therapy is tailored based on specific predisposing factors such as age, head trauma, neurosurgical history, or the presence of a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunt. Below are the detailed recommendations for each scenario: Age < 1 month Common causative pathogens: Streptococcus agalactiae, Escherichia coli, Listeria monocytogenes, Klebsiella species. Preferred regimen: Ampicillin 12 g/day IV every 4 hours AND One of the following: Cefotaxime 8–12 g/day IV every 4–6 hours Amikacin 15 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours Gentamicin 5 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours Tobramycin 5 mg/kg/day IV every 8 hours. Age 1–23 months Common causative pathogens: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus agalactiae, Haemophilus influenzae, Escherichia coli. Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND One of the following: Ceftriaxone 4 g IV every 12–24 hours Cefotaxime 8–12 g/day IV every 4–6 hours. Age 2–50 years Common causative pathogens: Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae. Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND One of the following: Ceftriaxone 4 g IV every 12–24 hours Cefotaxime 8–12 g/day IV every 4–6 hours. Age > 50 years Common causative pathogens: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Listeria monocytogenes, aerobic Gram-negative bacilli. Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND Ampicillin 12 g/day IV every 4 hours AND One of the following: Ceftriaxone 4 g IV every 12–24 hours Cefotaxime 8–12 g/day IV every 4–6 hours. Head trauma Basilar skull fracture Common causative pathogens: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, group A β-hemolytic streptococci. Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND One of the following: Ceftriaxone 4 g IV every 12–24 hours Cefotaxime 8–12 g/day IV every 4–6 hours. Penetrating trauma Common causative pathogens: Staphylococcus aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci (especially Staphylococcus epidermidis), aerobic Gram-negative bacilli (including Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND One of the following: Cefepime 6 g/day IV every 8 hours Ceftazidime 6 g/day IV every 8 hours Meropenem 6 g/day IV every 8 hours. Post-neurosurgery Common causative pathogens: Aerobic Gram-negative bacilli (including Pseudomonas aeruginosa), Staphylococcus aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci (especially Staphylococcus epidermidis). Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND One of the following: Cefepime 6 g/day IV every 8 hours Ceftazidime 6 g/day IV every 8 hours Meropenem 6 g/day IV every 8 hours. CSF shunt Common causative pathogens: Coagulase-negative staphylococci (especially Staphylococcus epidermidis), Staphylococcus aureus, aerobic Gram-negative bacilli (including Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Preferred regimen: Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day IV every 8–12 hours AND One of the following: Cefepime 6 g/day IV every 8 hours Ceftazidime 6 g/day IV every 8 hours Meropenem 6 g/day IV every 8 hours.
